Description
The Austrian Philharmonic Gold coin is the most popular coin series from the European continent.
Austrian Philharmonic Gold coins
were first released in 1989 in the hopes to honor the greatness that is the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra. Although these Austrian Gold coins have a face value of $100, they are worth a great deal more for their high gold content. This 1 oz  Austrian Philharmonic Gold coin is a highly recognizable, stunning, and precious gold coin that can strengthen your precious metal portfolio.
Like many of the other Austrian coins that are on the market today, the Philharmonic coins represent an incredible investment as well as an artistic piece. This 1 oz Austrian Philharmonic Gold coin is struck with 1 troy oz of .9999 pure gold. Since these coins have such a good quantity of pure gold in them, they are mostly used for investment purposes by people who are looking to hedge against inflation or convert their wealth to an easily transferred form of wealth. The year of mintage of the 1 oz Austrian Philharmonic Gold Coin may vary depending on the availability of the coin in our inventory.
Design of 1 oz Austrian Philharmonic Gold Coin
The Austrian Philharmonic Gold coin is a design masterpiece. The obverse of the 1 oz Austrian Philharmonic Gold coin features the depiction of the Great Organ of the Golden Hall in one of Austria’s most famous concert halls, the Musikverein. Above the great organ of the coin, is the inscription of  “REPUBLIK OSTERREICH” which means “The Republic of Austria” in English. Below the Great Organ, you can see “ 1 UNZE GOLD 999.9” along with the year of issue and denomination.
On the reverse of the 1 oz Austrian Gold Philharmonic Gold coin, you can see the depiction of an array of musical instruments carved in great detail. The musical instruments include a french horn, bassoon, harp, cello, and four violins. The inscription of the phrase “WIENER PHILHARMONIKER” can be seen just above the musical instruments.
